title: Evaluation metrics: correctness, format, tone and safety

videos.script: A test set gives you a number. This lesson asks which number. {{title}} Start with correctness. The prompt sorts forty-five of seventy messages correctly. That sentence hides where the other twenty-five went. A confusion matrix shows every one of them, label against label. {{matrix}} From it you read precision and recall. Billing is almost never said, and returns has become a catch-all. Twenty-two of thirty normal messages are marked urgent, and not one urgent message is marked normal. {{urgent}} Format is counted apart, so a reply that does not parse never looks like a wrong opinion. {{format}} Then tone. Forty replies from the model meet a handful of rules: exclamation marks, length, phrases the shop never uses, promises it cannot keep. Nineteen of them promise something. The rules miss one deadline and flag two replies that are perfectly fine, and eleven replies open with a placeholder no rule was looking for. {{tone}} Last, a prompt that wins on every total, and sends the billing team three tickets that are not theirs. {{many}} By the end you report metrics side by side, and you know which mistakes cost the most. {{close}}
